name: twinny
displayName: twinny - AI Code Completion and Chat
description: AI code completion, chat, inline edit and code review on models you run. Private, open source, one gateway for the whole team.

twinny.enabled.markdownDescription: Toggles the Twinny extension on or off. When `true`, Twinny is active and ready to provide completions.

twinny.enabledLanguages.markdownDescription:
Specifies which languages to enable completions with Twinny for. Use `*` as the default for all languages. Example:
```json
{
  "*": true,
  "python": true,
  "javascript": false
}
```

twinny.locale.markdownDescription: Sets the locale for Twinny. The default is `en` (English).

twinny.autoSuggestEnabled.markdownDescription: When `true`, Twinny will automatically suggest completions. You can still manually trigger completions using the default shortcut (`Alt+\`).

twinny.contentHash.algorithm.description: Algorithm used by editing and workspace indexing for self-describing content fingerprints.

twinny.indexing.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable Twinny's persistent workspace index in extension-managed storage, separate from durable TODO data.

twinny.indexing.auto.markdownDescription: Automatically synchronize the workspace index on activation and relevant workspace changes.

twinny.indexing.include.markdownDescription: Workspace-relative glob patterns eligible for indexing.

twinny.indexing.exclude.markdownDescription: Additional workspace-relative glob patterns excluded from indexing. Dependencies, generated output, binaries, and common credential files are excluded by default.

twinny.indexing.maxFileSize.description: Maximum file size in bytes for indexing. Larger files are reported as skipped.

twinny.contextLength.markdownDescription: Specifies how many lines of context (before and after the current line) to include in Fill-in-Middle (FIM) prompts. A higher number provides more context but may slow down completions.

twinny.debounceWait.markdownDescription: Sets the delay (in milliseconds) before triggering the next completion. This helps reduce API calls and improve performance.

twinny.temperature.markdownDescription: Controls the randomness of code completions. Lower values (e.g., 0.2) produce more focused and deterministic completions, while higher values (e.g., 0.8) lead to more diverse ones. Chat, inline edit and code review send no temperature; the server's default applies.

twinny.multilineCompletionsEnabled.markdownDescription: When `true`, Twinny will attempt to generate multi-line completions. This is an experimental feature and may not work perfectly in all scenarios.

twinny.maxLines.markdownDescription: Sets the maximum number of lines for multi-line completions. Only applies when `twinny.multilineCompletionsEnabled` is `true`.

twinny.fileContextEnabled.markdownDescription: When `true`, Twinny will scan neighboring documents to provide more context for completions. This is an experimental feature and may impact performance.

twinny.recentEditsEnabled.markdownDescription: Shows the model the last few changes you made, in any open file, as short diffs. A half-done rename or a pattern being applied across a file then carries into completions. Up to 6 changes and 2,500 characters.

twinny.lspContextEnabled.markdownDescription: Includes matching IntelliSense symbols and available type signatures in FIM context. Uses installed completion providers, with up to 20 suggestions, 2,000 characters and a 150 ms wait limit. Works independently of file context.

twinny.completionCacheEnabled.markdownDescription: Enables caching of Fill-in-Middle (FIM) completions for identical prompts. This can significantly improve performance but may use more memory.

twinny.numPredictFim.markdownDescription: Defines the maximum number of tokens for Fill-in-Middle (FIM) completions. Use `-1` for no limit. Twinny will attempt to stop at logical line breaks regardless of this setting.

twinny.enableSubsequentCompletions.markdownDescription: When `true`, Twinny will continue to make completion requests to the API after the previous completion was accepted. This can provide a more fluid completion experience.

twinny.embeddingIgnoredGlobs.markdownDescription: Extra file patterns to skip when building embeddings, such as `**/*.md` or `**/fixtures/**`. Only source, config and documentation files are indexed to begin with; binaries such as fonts and images are always skipped.

twinny.embeddingUpdateOnSave.description: Keep the workspace index current: re-embed a file when it is saved and forget it when it is deleted. Only applies once the workspace has been indexed.

twinny.ollamaHostname.markdownDescription: Specifies the hostname for the Ollama API. Use `0.0.0.0` for localhost or provide a specific IP address or domain name.

twinny.ollamaApiPort.markdownDescription: Sets the port number for the Ollama API. The default is `11434`, but you can change it if your Ollama instance uses a different port.

twinny.p2pPort.markdownDescription: UDP port this computer listens on when sharing its Ollama with paired devices (Providers → Devices → Share). Devices on your network connect to this port, so a firewall on this computer must allow it, e.g. `sudo ufw allow 49737/udp`. Takes effect the next time sharing starts.

twinny.teamShareSlots.markdownDescription: How many teammates' requests this computer runs at once while sharing it with the team (Providers → Share this computer). Takes effect the next time sharing starts.

twinny.keepAlive.markdownDescription: Sets the duration to keep models in memory for Ollama API. Use formats like `5m` for 5 minutes or `1h` for 1 hour. Set to `-1` to keep models in memory indefinitely.

twinny.warmUpModel.markdownDescription: Load the completion model when VS Code starts or regains focus, so the first completion does not wait for a cold model. Only for local model servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp); hosted APIs are never called.

twinny.ollamaUseTls.markdownDescription: When `true`, Twinny will use TLS encryption for connections to the Ollama API. Ensure your Ollama instance is configured for TLS before enabling this option.

enumDescriptions: Redact credentials in prompts sent to anything that is not on this machine: hosted APIs, a Twinny gateway, a paired device, a server elsewhere on the network.
Redact credentials in every prompt, local servers included.
twinny.secretShield.markdownDescription: **Secret shield.** API keys, tokens, private keys and passwords in a prompt (your question, attached files, the code around the cursor) are replaced with placeholders like `REDACTED_GITHUB_TOKEN_1` before the request is sent, and put back wherever the reply repeats a placeholder. The model never sees the value; the chat shows how many were withheld. Detection covers well-known token formats, private key blocks, passwords in URLs, and secret-named values in code and `.env` files.

twinny.enableLogging.markdownDescription: Writes what Twinny is doing to the **Twinny** output channel: one line per completion or chat request with model, timing, size and why it stopped. Set the channel's log level to *Debug* (the dropdown in the Output panel) to also see the prompts and replies. Warnings and errors are written even when this is off.

twinny.chatSuggestions.markdownDescription: Shows grey text ahead of the cursor in the chat composer; `Tab` accepts it and `Ctrl+→` accepts a word of it. It finishes words from what you have typed before, as a phone keyboard does, and once a conversation has an exchange, a pause after a word asks the chat model for the rest of the message given the last few turns. No requests are made while a reply is coming.

twinny.agents.markdownDescription: Selectable Copilot-compatible .agent.md profiles. Twinny discovers .github/agents in each workspace and its extension global storage agents directory. MCP entries are references to servers already configured in twinny.chatToolsMcpServers; definitions in agent files are never executed. The agent a new chat starts with is set by `#twinny.agents.startupSelection#`.

defaultSelection.deprecationMessage: Deprecated: use twinny.agents.startupSelection to choose the agent a new chat starts with.
defaultSelection.description: Deprecated and no longer read. Use twinny.agents.startupSelection.

autoDiscover.description: Discover .agent.md profiles in workspace .github/agents and extension global storage.

searchPaths.description: Additional directories containing .agent.md files. Supports ${workspaceFolder}/ and ${extensionGlobalStorage}/ prefixes.

ignoreAgentToolRestrictions.markdownDescription: Ignore tools declared in .agent.md profiles and use Twinny's normally available tools instead.

enumDescriptions: Start a new chat with Agent off.
Start a new chat with Default Agent.
Start a new chat with the agent last chosen from the agent picker or with Shift+Tab. If that custom profile is missing or disabled, Default Agent is used.
twinny.agents.startupSelection.markdownDescription: Which agent a new chat starts with. Only new chats and the New chat command use this; a chat that is already open keeps its agent. Choosing Agent off yourself does not change this setting.

twinny.chatTools.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Lets the chat model work in the workspace: find, read and search files (by regular expression, and by meaning through the embeddings index), read git history, ask the language servers for errors, references and definitions, edit, create, rename, move and delete files, and run commands. Edits are applied straight away unless `#twinny.chatToolsEdits#` asks for review; each applied edit comes back with any errors the editor then reports in the file, and the reply ends with the files it changed, each of which can be compared with what it was or undone. Commands ask first unless `#twinny.chatToolsCommands#` says otherwise. The project's `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) is followed, and a folder's own `AGENTS.md` once the model works there. Files ignored by a `.gitignore` are off limits, and changes to `.vscode/`, a `.gitignore` or an `AGENTS.md` are always shown for review. Each step shows in the reply at the point it ran. Needs a capable coder model such as `qwen3-coder:30b` with a context of 8k tokens or more; small models tend to call tools badly. Set in your user settings; a workspace cannot turn it on.

twinny.chatBaseInstructionsMode.markdownDescription: Select the optional conversational chat base instructions. Custom Markdown is read on each new request; None omits this layer without disabling runtime context, tools, or application policies.

twinny.chatBaseInstructionsFile.markdownDescription: Path to the custom Markdown file used when Chat Base Instructions is set to Custom Markdown File.

twinny.feedback.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable **Feedback**: Twinny plans TODOs from your agent requests, tracks task progress and tool evidence, independently evaluates completed work and reconciles what remains. Works with ordinary and compiled prompts alike and never depends on the Prompt Compiler. Replaces `#twinny.chatToolsFeedbackEvaluatorEnabled#`.

twinny.feedback.provider.markdownDescription: Provider used by Feedback for TODO planning and evaluation, given as a provider ID or label from Twinny's providers panel. Leave empty to use the provider selected for **Feedback** in the providers panel. An unknown provider is reported as an error; Twinny never switches to another provider on its own.

twinny.feedback.model.markdownDescription: Model used by Feedback. Leave empty to use the model configured on the Feedback provider.

twinny.promptCompiler.enabled.markdownDescription: Make the **Prompt Compiler** available. When enabled, Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click on macOS) the Send button to rewrite the composer draft into a clearer prompt. The result replaces the draft for you to review, edit, discard or send; it is never sent automatically, and a plain Send always sends your text as written. When disabled, Ctrl/Cmd+Click sends normally. Replaces `#twinny.chatToolsIntentCompilerEnabled#`.

twinny.promptCompiler.provider.markdownDescription: Provider used by the Prompt Compiler, given as a provider ID or label from Twinny's providers panel. Leave empty to use the provider selected for **Feedback** in the providers panel. Compiler failures never affect Feedback or TODOs.

twinny.promptCompiler.model.markdownDescription: Model used by the Prompt Compiler. Leave empty to use the model configured on the Prompt Compiler's provider.

twinny.promptCompiler.maxTurns.markdownDescription: How many previous prompt/response turns the Prompt Compiler may read as context when rewriting a draft. Set to `0` to use only the draft.

twinny.promptCompiler.trace.markdownDescription: Write the raw Prompt Compiler request and provider response to a local trace file under the extension storage folder for debugging. Disabled by default; the file may contain workspace or conversation content.

twinny.promptCompiler.baseInstructionsMo.markdownDescription: Base instructions for the Prompt Compiler, independent of chat instructions. Twinny's response format remains enforced when this is None or customized.

twinny.promptCompiler.baseInstructionsFi.markdownDescription: Path to the custom Markdown file used when Prompt Compiler base instructions are set to `custom`.

twinny.chatToolsFeedbackEvaluatorEnabled.markdownDeprecationMessage: Replaced by `#twinny.feedback.enabled#`. An explicitly set value is still honoured until the new setting is set.

twinny.chatToolsIntentCompilerEnabled.markdownDeprecationMessage: Replaced by `#twinny.promptCompiler.enabled#`, which only makes the compiler available on Ctrl/Cmd+Click Send.

twinny.chatToolsIntentCompilerMode.markdownDeprecationMessage: Retired and ignored. The Prompt Compiler never runs automatically; Ctrl/Cmd+Click Send compiles the draft into the composer without sending it.

twinny.chatToolsAdaptiveExposureEnabled.markdownDescription: Reduce MCP tools sent to chat agent turns using deterministic task-capability matching. Disabled by default; when disabled, the authorized Tool Picker selection is exposed unchanged. This never grants tools or changes approval settings.

twinny.chatToolsReconciliationMaxIterati.markdownDescription: Maximum Feedback reconciliation and automatic continuation turns for one agent task.

twinny.chatToolsReconciliationMaxNoProgr.markdownDescription: Stop automatic execution after this many consecutive turns without verified file progress.

twinny.chatToolsRegressionErrorSpike.markdownDescription: New language-server errors in one workspace edit that trigger automatic rollback.

twinny.chatToolsRegressionCumulativeErro.markdownDescription: Cumulative new errors threshold used with a single-edit increase of at least eight errors.

enumDescriptions: Edits go straight into the file and are saved; the model carries on until the task is done. Ctrl+Z in the file undoes an edit. Deleting a file git has no copy of still asks first.
Each edit opens as a diff to accept or reject, and the model stops until you have decided. Renames, moves and deletes ask in the chat.
twinny.chatToolsEdits.markdownDescription: What happens when the chat model changes a file (with `#twinny.chatTools#` on).

enumDescriptions: Each command the model wants to run is shown in the chat with Run, Always run and Skip first.
Commands run straight away. A command cannot be undone like an edit can.
twinny.chatToolsCommands.markdownDescription: Whether the chat model may run shell commands (tests, builds), with `#twinny.chatTools#` on. It sees the exit code and the end of the output. This sets where the **auto-run** switch in the chat's composer starts; once you switch it, the switch decides (`off` still turns commands off). Reading git (status, diff, log) never asks: it cannot change anything.

enabled.description: Whether Twinny may start this MCP server and offer its tools. Set to false to keep it disabled.

type.description: Transport type for a local stdio server. Omit it for the legacy config format.

command.description: The program that runs the server, e.g. npx or uvx.

env.description: Environment variables for it, on top of VS Code's.

cwd.description: The folder it runs in; the workspace root by default.

enabled.description: Whether Twinny may start this MCP server and offer its tools. Set to false to keep it disabled.

url.description: The streamable MCP HTTP endpoint, e.g. http://localhost:3000/mcp or https://example.com/mcp.

headers.description: HTTP headers for the server request, such as Authorization: Bearer ... or custom headers.

timeoutMs.description: How long Twinny waits for an HTTP response before failing the request.

twinny.chatToolsMcpServers.markdownDescription: Model Context Protocol servers whose tools agent mode can use (with `#twinny.chatTools#` on), by name: `{ "github": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer …" } } }`. Legacy stdio servers still work with `{ "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"], "env": { "GITHUB_TOKEN": "…" } }`. Set `enabled: false` to keep a server disabled. Each call is shown with Run and Skip first, unless you chose Always run for that tool or enabled `twinny.mcpNeverAskAgain`. Every tool goes into every agent request, so a server with many tools makes small models pick worse. Set in your user settings; a workspace cannot add one.

twinny.mcpNeverAskAgain.title: MCP: Never ask me. EVER.
twinny.mcpNeverAskAgain.markdownDescription: Automatically approve every tool call from enabled MCP servers. Applies across conversations and restarts. Does not enable disabled servers or override external system permissions. This includes destructive actions offered by enabled servers.

twinny.chatContextFallback.markdownDescription: The context size, in tokens, to plan chat requests for when no server confirms the model's context (with `#twinny.chatContextWindow#` on Auto). It is an assumption, not a confirmed capacity, and the chat says so with a warning.

twinny.chatContextWindow.markdownDescription: The context size, in tokens, for chat requests. `Auto` asks the provider's server for the model's context, and uses the smallest size it confirms. A number sets the size yourself and is used as given, which is useful for testing small windows. Agent work needs 65536 tokens; a smaller size is reported with a warning.

twinny.chatToolsMaxSteps.markdownDescription: How many tool steps one agent reply may take before the model is asked to answer with what it has (with `#twinny.chatTools#` on). More lets a capable model finish longer tasks in one reply; each step is another request to the model.

twinny.chatInferenceMaxDurationSeconds.markdownDescription: The longest one model request may run, in seconds, before `#twinny.chatTools#` stops it and keeps the completed tool results. `0` turns this limit off.

twinny.chatInferenceNoProgressSeconds.markdownDescription: How long a model request may send no output, in seconds, before it is stopped as stalled. `0` turns this limit off.

twinny.chatInferenceMaxOutputTokens.markdownDescription: Output tokens asked of the server for each model request. The default is `6144`; `0` keeps the server's own limit. A request that reaches it is stopped, and a tool call it was still writing is not run.

twinny.chatToolsMaxReadLines.markdownDescription: The maximum number of lines any single `read_file` call may return. Lower values keep tool results smaller; higher values let the agent read wider ranges in one pass. A read longer than this is refused with suggested ranges rather than cut short.

twinny.chatToolsAllowFullFileReadsBeyond.markdownDescription: Allow a whole-file `read_file` (one given only a path, or with `full_file` set to `true`) to return more lines than `twinny.chatToolsMaxReadLines`. Off by default. Ranges stay bounded by `twinny.chatToolsMaxReadLines`. A whole file this large uses much more of the model's context.

twinny.chatToolsMaxResultChars.markdownDescription: The largest tool-result payload kept in a model's context before the agent trims older results. This scales with the model's context window while never exceeding the cap.

enumDescriptions: Each command runs in a process of its own through your shell, from the workspace root. Its output shows in the chat as it prints. Nothing can answer a prompt, and it is stopped after two minutes.
Commands run in the **twinny tools** terminal, which opens beside the editor, so you can watch and type into them. Needs VS Code's shell integration; without it they run in the background.
twinny.chatToolsCommandsRunIn.markdownDescription: Where the chat model's commands run (with `#twinny.chatToolsCommands#` not `off`).

twinny.githubToken.markdownDescription: Your personal GitHub access token. This is used for fetching data from GitHub repositories. Keep this token secure and do not share it.

twinny.providerStorageLocation.markdownDescription: Specifies where to store Twinny provider configurations. 'globalState' uses VS Code's global state (persists per domain, may be lost if domain changes frequently). 'file' stores configurations in a file within the extension's global storage directory (more resilient to domain changes).

twinny.reviewMaxDiffChars.description: Characters of diff sent to the model per code-review request. Larger reviews are split into parts. Lower this for models with small context windows; raise it for large-context models to get fewer parts.

scripts.pretest: npm run clean && npm run build-tests && npm run build && npm run lint
